item.title: Mt. Chokai (Dewa Fuji): Akita's Coastal Volcano — Guide
item.description: Mt. Chokai is a majestic 2,236 m volcano rising straight from the coast on the Akita–Yamagata border — the ‘Dewa Fuji’. Its upper slopes hold alpine meadows and snow patches into summer, and clear-day panoramas sweep across the Sea of Japan. Multiple trails climb from both prefectures; the Akita-side Hokodate route is popular in the July–September season. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Nikaho, Akita Hours Hiking season ~Jul–Sep Admission Free Time needed Full day (summit) Best time Summer (alpine flowers) What to See The 2,236 m ‘Dewa Fuji’ rising from the coast.

item.title: Mt. Moriyoshi: Akita's Snow Monsters & Ropeway — Guide
item.description: Mt. Moriyoshi (1,454 m) in Kitaakita is a gentle peak reached by ropeway, famed for two very different seasons — winter ‘snow monsters’ (juhyo), fir trees encased in wind-sculpted rime ice, and summer carpets of alpine flowers across the highland. The ropeway makes both spectacles accessible without a hard climb. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Kitaakita, Akita Hours Ropeway seasonal (winter & green season) Admission Ropeway fee applies Time needed 2–3 hours Best time Feb (snow monsters); summer flowers What to See Winter ‘snow monsters’ (juhyo) of rime-encased firs.

item.title: Tazawako Highland Hiking: Komagatake & Lake Views — Guide
item.description: The mountains surrounding Lake Tazawa offer some of Akita’s finest hiking. Akita Komagatake (1,637 m) rises directly from the lake’s caldera rim, with sweeping views over the cobalt water to the Ou Mountains beyond. The route from the Hachigome trailhead is the most popular, taking 3–4 hours return, with alpine flowers in summer. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Tazawako, Senboku, Akita Hours Hiking season ~Jun–Oct Admission Free (shuttle bus fee) Time needed 3–4 hours (Komagatake) Best time Summer (alpine flowers); autumn What to See Akita Komagatake (1,637 m) above the caldera rim.
